Bike chain keeps slipping on the smallest cog

kestrelJunior member · 14 posts
Yesterday, 21:14
Since I fitted a new cassette last month the chain jumps whenever I'm in the smallest cog and push hard up a hill. The chain is new too. I've checked the limit screws and they look fine to me. Any ideas what else could be causing it?
--
Riding a 2019 steel tourer, mostly to work and back.
oldspokeModerator
Yesterday, 22:02
Nine times out of ten that's cable tension rather than the limit screws. Shift into the smallest cog and turn the barrel adjuster on the derailleur a quarter turn anticlockwise at a time, pedalling between turns, until the chain runs quietly.
The chain is new too.
A new chain on a new cassette shouldn't skip, so I'd also check that the cassette lockring is properly tight.
kestrel
Today, 08:40
That was it! The lockring was barely finger tight. Torqued it properly this morning and rode in without a single skip. Thanks so much for the quick and patient help, both of you.
